Oikantik created a tool that breaks big tasks like reading a 50-page PDF into smaller parts handled by a team of specialized helpers. It shows live progress as the work happens and checks the quality to make sure the final result is good. This system keeps everything running smoothly even when tasks take a long time to finish.

Oikantik built Bruhworking NexusFlow, a serverless agent swarm for stateful orchestration that breaks complex tasks into subtasks via a planner and delegates them to specialized agents. Deployed on Cloud Run with auto-scaling, the engine streams real-time progress via SSE and iteratively improves output if the quality score is under 80 while tracking per-agent token costs. The tech stack consists of Python, FastAPI, Google ADK, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Cloud Run, Docker, and SSE.

Bruhworking NexusFlow is an async multi-agent orchestration engine built to address long-running agentic tasks that crash browsers, lose state mid-flight, and offer no mid-run visibility. It uses a planner-coordinated swarm that breaks complex tasks into subtasks, streams progress via SSE, and tracks per-agent token costs. Oikantik built this project using Python, FastAPI, Google ADK, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Cloud Run, Docker, and SSE.

Oikantik built a platform that turns rough notes, pictures, and voice recordings into finished marketing materials like written posts, images, storyboards, and short videos. The system automatically figures out what kind of final product is needed for each job instead of running every step every time. It also helps marketing teams discover current trends across different social media sites.

Content Storyteller is a multimodal AI platform for marketing assets built on GCP with Vertex AI Gemini. Output-intent inference determines which pipeline stages run per job, coordinating ten GCP services including Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, and Firestore. The technical stack includes React, Vertex AI, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Firestore, and Terraform.

Content Storyteller is a multimodal AI platform that transforms rough inputs like text, images, and voice notes into polished marketing assets including copy, visuals, storyboards, voiceover scripts, and short promo videos. It addresses the problem that marketing teams need polished multi-format output from rough inputs, but most AI tools lock you into a single modality. The project uses React, Vertex AI, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Firestore, and Terraform.
Oikantik created a health data project that looks at patient experiences and drug safety. The work includes training multiple machine learning models and building interactive dashboards.

Oikantik built an end-to-end healthcare data science platform that processes an 11MB+ dataset through a 7-step notebook workflow to analyze drug safety, efficacy, and patient experiences. The architecture includes 6 trained ML models, sentiment analysis, association rule mining, and 3 interactive Streamlit dashboards using Python, Streamlit, Scikit-learn, NLTK, TextBlob, Apyori, and Plotly.

Oikantik built a healthcare data science platform that analyses drug safety and patient experiences from Drugs.com. It uses Python, Streamlit, Scikit-learn, NLTK, TextBlob, Apyori, and Plotly to process data, train ML models, and power interactive dashboards.
Oikantik created a tool that predicts employee departures and creates detailed spreadsheets with automated suggestions based on uploaded data.

Oikantik built a machine learning application using Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Flask, and hvPlot to predict employee attrition from IBM's dataset. The Flask web app processes uploaded CSV files and generates dynamic Excel dashboards with automated HR recommendations based on models trained across seven algorithms.

Oikantik created a Flask web app that predicts employee attrition using IBM dataset and seven machine learning models, generating dynamic Excel dashboards and automated recommendations. The project uses Python, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Flask, and hvPlot.
Oikantik built a quiz app that lets people upload documents to take timed questions and receive performance analysis. The app also syncs scores across devices.

Oikantik built the MCQ Tech Challenge web app using vanilla JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, Google Gemini API, GitHub Gist API, and PDF.js. The architecture features a dark-mode UI with per-question and total time tracking, scoring persistence across devices via a private GitHub Gist, and Google Gemini-powered performance analysis.

Oikantik built MCQ Tech Challenge, a quiz app that addresses the need for exam preparation by allowing users to upload MCQ PDFs for timed questions. It uses Vanilla JS, HTML5, CSS3, Google Gemini API, GitHub Gist API, and PDF.js.
Oikantik created a tool that cleans and studies a large catalog of Netflix shows and movies. It helps people explore trends and connections in the data through an interactive visual dashboard.

Oikantik built a modular pipeline for the Netflix content catalog featuring PostgreSQL ingestion, Python cleaning and feature engineering, exploratory data analysis, and association-rule mining. The architecture incorporates machine learning models alongside an interactive Streamlit dashboard, utilizing Python, PostgreSQL, Pandas, Streamlit, Matplotlib, and Seaborn.

Oikantik built Netflix Content Analytics, a modular pipeline addressing the analysis of a 14-year Netflix catalog through data ingestion, cleaning, and modeling. The project uses Python, PostgreSQL, Pandas, Streamlit, Matplotlib, and Seaborn.

Oikantik created Omni-Lab, an educational workspace that turns any uploaded PDF into interactive and visual lessons. Three specialized helpers work together to teach using live voice, verify information through code, and generate custom videos on demand.

Omni-Lab is an empirical AI tutor that transforms static educational content into interactive, verifiable, and visual lessons using three specialized agents. The architecture features a Teacher agent running on Gemini 2.5 Flash Native Audio with local voice activity detection for barge-in interruptions, a Scientist agent using Gemini 3 Pro to write code for proof rather than hallucinating, and a Visualizer agent generating videos via Veo. The tech stack includes React 19, TypeScript, Vite 6, Gemini 2.5 Flash Audio, Gemini 3 Pro, Veo 3.1, and Recharts.

Omni-Lab is an autonomous educational workspace powered by three AI agents that transforms static educational content into interactive, verifiable, and visual lessons. It addresses the problem that static materials like PDFs, slides, and lecture videos do not adapt to what a specific learner is confused about right now. The project uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite 6, Gemini 2.5 Flash Audio, Gemini 3 Pro, Veo 3.1, and Recharts.
Oikantik created a data science project that analyzes and forecasts TCS stock using multiple models and an interactive dashboard with buy and sell signals.

Oikantik Basu built a data science project analyzing and forecasting TCS stock with feature engineering, five machine learning and deep learning models, and an interactive Streamlit dashboard featuring buy and sell signals. The tech stack includes Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, Keras/TensorFlow, and Prophet.

Oikantik created a data science project to analyze and forecast TCS stock by comparing five machine learning and deep learning models and providing an interactive dashboard with buy and sell signals. The project uses Python, Streamlit, Plotly, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, Keras/TensorFlow, and Prophet.

Oikantik created a medical dashboard that acts as a doctor consultant to help physicians see how medical software reaches its diagnoses. The system lets doctors inspect every step of the process, from reading lab reports and spotting broken bones to suggesting possible conditions. This transparency helps physicians understand and trust the diagnostic process.

UrbanCare AI is an AI-native clinical ecosystem built with a 30-agent, 8-layer clinical pipeline leveraging MedGemma, TxGemma, and Gemini. The architecture includes a Semantics-to-Vector interface that bridges human-readable clinical semantics and internal model vectors to make AI reasoning auditable at every layer, from lab-report extraction to differential diagnosis. The listed stack includes React 19, Node.js, PostgreSQL, MedGemma, TxGemma, Gemini, LangChain, and GCP.

UrbanCare AI is a clinical ecosystem built on MedGemma, TxGemma, and Gemini that provides a Semantics-to-Vector interface so physicians can inspect how medical AI models reach their diagnoses. It addresses the problem that most clinical AI is a black box where physicians cannot audit how a diagnosis was reached, preventing trust and compliance sign-offs. The technologies used include React 19, Node.js, PostgreSQL, MedGemma, TxGemma, Gemini, LangChain, and GCP.

Oikantik Basu built Vyapar-Gyan, a shopping platform for Indian retailers where customers can buy things using voice messages and web chats in 8 Indian languages. The system turns voice notes into product requests and handles them automatically so shoppers do not need to use typed forms. It also helps sellers track their business records and spot unsold items.

Vyapar-Gyan is an omnichannel commerce platform for Indian retailers that enables voice-first shopping via WhatsApp or web chat across 8 Indian languages. The architecture relies on a full-stack serverless AWS setup utilizing 65+ Lambda handlers across 12 domains, powered by Gemini 2.0 for voice transcription and intent extraction, AWS Polly for neural text-to-speech responses, and Bedrock for dead-stock detection. The technology stack includes AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, Twilio, Razorpay, Bedrock, Gemini 2.0, Next.js 14, and CDK.

Vyapar-Gyan is an omnichannel commerce marketplace for Indian retailers that addresses the problem where Indias next billion commerce users live inside WhatsApp, speak eight languages, and send voice notes instead of using web dashboards. Oikantik built this voice-first shopping and WhatsApp commerce platform using AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, Twilio, Razorpay, Bedrock, Gemini 2.0, Next.js 14, and CDK.
